baseline.holdoutRule: The v1-v14 holdouts were promoted to regression after evaluation. The v13 traveller image remains not_sure: pixel review of the exact submitted JPEG established that its circular 10-cent shape and barcode survive, but SG/RETURN does not, so source-page context cannot supply the missing jurisdiction evidence. Every complete run fails before any model call when two declared sources reach 0.995 perceptual similarity. The two v15 holdouts are previously unused real-network visuals selected, pixel-reviewed, truth-labelled and frozen before either was submitted to the production or candidate profile: one real close-up shows a readable Singapore Deposit Mark and unobscured linear product barcode on the same individual can; one retail catalogue composite places a standalone Deposit Mark beside a front-facing bottle whose product barcode is not shown, so the composite cannot establish same-container eligibility. They are developer-visible, non-adaptive holdouts rather than an independently sealed or blinded evaluation set, and must not be used to revise and re-score the same candidate.

invariants: Only containers carrying the BCRS Deposit Mark are eligible for a refund.
The refund is S$0.10 per eligible container.
Containers without the mark remain recyclable through blue bins or other recycling stations.
The scheme product-approval guide distinguishes the product barcode from the separate square 2D traceability code printed on some approved labels.
